Yes. For a small Toronto beauty salon, I’d look for someone who can handle both content and the enquiry/booking side, rather than just posting pretty photos.

Here are the strongest fits I found:

Social Influenc. Agency — Toronto agency with social-media management, content direction, Instagram/Facebook marketing, and a specific focus on appointment-based businesses. This looks particularly relevant if you want Instagram + generating appointment enquiries.

Qode Social Media Agency — Offers content creation, Instagram/social management, engagement, and ongoing optimization. They also advertise a free social-media audit.

Social Media 55 — Full-service social management including content creation and community management, so they can help with the comments/DM side as well.

The Influence Agency — Larger Toronto agency covering Instagram, TikTok, influencer marketing, paid social and broader digital marketing. Better if you're looking for a more comprehensive growth partner.

Reel Time Creations — Particularly interesting for beauty businesses: they shoot content on-site, create Reels/photos/stories, manage posting and comments/DMs, and explicitly measure booking conversions. 
Reel Time Creations

BBMedia — Specifically markets to Toronto/GTA beauty salons, with Instagram/Xiaohongshu content, beauty influencer/KOL campaigns and booking-focused advertising. 
BrandBoosty

The Salon Marketing Company — More salon-specific and potentially more budget-friendly; its site currently advertises Instagram growth and Meta advertising starting around $129/month, although I'd verify exactly what's included before comparing it with full-service agencies. 
Salon Marketing Co.
+1

My shortlist for your situation

If you mainly need someone to take Instagram off your plate: Reel Time Creations.
If appointment enquiries/DMs are the priority: Social Influenc. Agency or Reel Time Creations.
If you're a traditional hair/beauty salon rather than a med spa: BBMedia or The Salon Marketing Company are worth investigating.
If you want a larger, full-service marketing partner: The Influence Agency.

One thing I'd specifically ask each provider: “Will you actually respond to Instagram DMs and turn enquiries into bookings, or do you only create/post content?” Those are quite different services.

If you tell me roughly how much you want to spend per month (e.g. under $500, $500–$1,500, or $1,500+), I can narrow this to 3 Toronto options that fit a small salon's budget, including what each appears to offer.
